articles.title: 2026 NYC Marathon: Date, start time, route, how to watch and everything you need to know about the prestigious race
articles.summary: The weather in New York City should be perfect on marathon day.
articles.body:
On Sunday, over two million fans will line up on the streets of New York City to support the roughly 60,000 runners in the 2026 NYC Marathon. The action gets underway at 8 a.m. ET.

This year will mark the 56th time the race has taken place. After winning the event for the second time last year, women's champ Hellen Obiri will go for her third NYC Marathon win. On the men's side Benson Kipruto will look to become the first man to go back-to-back at the event since Geoffery Mutai did it in 2011 and 2013 (the 2012 NYC Marathon was canceled due to Hurricane Sandy).

With the event fast approaching, here's everything you need to know about the 2026 NYC Marathon.

The 2026 NYC Marathon will take place Sunday, Nov. 1. The first batch of competitors will start at 8 a.m. ET.

When the race first started in 1970, it was run in September. But that shifted in 1976, when the NYC Marathon was shifted to late October. Ten years later, the marathon was moved to the first Sunday in November. It's remained on that schedule since 1986.

The men's professional wheelchair division will kick things off at 8 a.m. ET. They'll be followed by the women's professional wheelchair division at 8:02 a.m. ET and then the handcycles and select athletes with disabilities group at 8:22 a.m. ET.

At 8:35 a.m. ET, the professional women's division will begin. A half hour later, the professional men will take the course.

Starting at 9:10 a.m. ET, the first wave of runners will take the course. Every 35 minutes after that, another wave will be released, with the last one starting at 11:30 a.m. ET.

This year will mark the first time in 15 years that the NYC Marathon course has changed.

As usual, the race will start in Staten Island and will run through all five boroughs of New York. The biggest adjustment this year will come after runners cross the Willis Avenue Bridge, which connects Manhattan to the Bronx. At that point, the course will diverge slightly before runners wind up back on track at the Madison Avenue Bridge.

It's not a massive change, but one that was made to " minimize the race's impacts on the Bronx ," per NYRR.org.

All eyes will be on Obiri and Kipruto in 2026. The defending champs will draw the most attention heading into the event, though a number of other contenders could give them a run for their money this year.

With a win, Obiri would take first in the race for the third time. Only three other women have won the NYC Marathon three times. Obiri did set the course record last year, so she's in a good spot to be in contention once again.

Kipruto narrowly took home the crown last year, with the race going to a photo finish . It was ultimately determined he finished ahead of Alexander Mutiso Munyao for the win. If Kiputo can win the event again in 2026, he would become the seventh man to win consecutive NYC Marathons.

It should be a lovely day for a marathon Sunday in New York City. The skies are expected to be partly cloudy for the event, with a high of 61 degrees. Sounds like the perfect day for a long run.

If you can't attend the event in person, you're in luck. The 2026 NYC Marathon will be available to watch in a few different spots .

Locally, the race will be broadcast on ABC7 from 8 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. ET.

Nationally, the event will air on ESPN2 during that same window. Spanish coverage can be found on ESPN3.

Later in the day, ABC will run a two-hour live show from the finish line that will show runners finishing the race. That will take place between 3 and 5 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Bold Fantasy Football Predictions for Week 8
articles.summary: The Yahoo Fantasy crew gets bold for Week 8.
articles.body:
Week 8 is in full swing after the Packers defeated the Panthers on TNF. With that, we await the rest of the slate. Here, our Yahoo analysts share their one bold prediction for Week 8 fantasy football.

Rookie Antonio Williams posts 70 yards and a TD in post-bye breakout

The Commanders have lost WR1 Terry McLaurin for the rest of this season and will come back from the bye with a reshuffled receiver corps. Dan Quinn already said that increasing Stefon Diggs' snaps will not be a part of that plan. They want to keep the veteran receiver fresh for the rest of the year. That means that rookie Antonio Williams is destined for a bump in his workload.

His tape has earned that promotion; he's been even more impressive on film so far than I expected, and I was a fan of his prospect profile. Williams looks explosive and separates against man coverage down the field. Washington needs a player like that to step up. Williams' mild coming-out party occurred in Week 1 against this same Eagles defense he faces on Sunday Night Football in Week 8. This will be an even bigger outing on a full complement of snaps.

He should see routes both inside and out. Philadelphia is vulnerable at the second corner spot opposite Quinyon Mitchell and gives up the fourth-most fantasy points to slot receivers so far. Williams can take advantage of both matchups. — Matt Harmon

Chase Brown silences haters, goes over 100 yards and scores

Brown has had a disappointing start to the season, failing to reach 85 scrimmage yards in any game so far. He also hasn't found the end zone since Week 1. I expect both those stats to change on Sunday, when Brown takes on a Titans defense that's allowed at least 85 yards to the last three starting running backs they've faced, including big performances the past two weeks from Quinshon Judkins (104 yards, two TDs) and Jonathan Taylor (151 yards, TD).

This spot got even better when news broke that Tennessee was trading its star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, removing his elite run-stopping from the equation. Despite Brown's struggles, he's still dominating touches and snaps in the Bengals' backfield. After a difficult opening stretch, which was almost entirely filled with challenging run defenses (Bucs, Texans, Steelers, Jaguars, Ravens), get ready for Brown to notch his first fantasy RB1 finish of the year in a much more generous Week 8 matchup. — Justin Boone

I realize two games are a small sample. But think about the other first-time QB-WR duos struggling to get it together. Drake Maye and A.J. Brown. Kyler Murray and Justin Jefferson. DJ Moore and Josh Allen didn't need long to click. In Week 1, Moore earned a 27% target share and 46% of the air yards. By Week 3, those numbers climbed to 38% and 52%, and his target rate on third and fourth downs jumped to 56%. He went straight to the top of the target tree.

The shoulder is the obvious question. However, assuming he's active, Baltimore is the right spot for his return. The Ravens defense has bottom-10 marks in yards per game allowed to WRs, passing success rate allowed and fantasy PPG allowed. Chris Olave (22.6 PPR points) and both of my Bengals receivers have feasted on this secondary, and even Carnell Tate went for 145 yards. With Baltimore forced to account for Allen's legs, Moore will remind us he's a top-12 receiver. — Chris Allen

Michael Wilson bounces back for over 100 yards and a touchdown

It's been a frustrating season for Michael Wilson managers, but the opportunity is there. He's running a route on 89.4% of Arizona's dropbacks, commanding 23.3% of team targets and drawing 29.5% of first-read targets. He's involved. Now, we need that usage to turn into production.

Dallas just allowed Makai Lemon to catch seven passes for 67 yards and a touchdown, while Tanner McKee threw for 211 yards and looked more than functional for stretches of that game. Nobody's calling that an overwhelming passing performance, but we watched an inexperienced quarterback and a rookie receiver find success against this defense.

Now Arizona gets a 54.5-point game total, tied for the highest on the slate, with Dallas favored by 7.5 points. Let's be honest: the Cardinals should be able to move the ball against this defense, and Dallas can score enough to keep Arizona throwing. Wilson's on the field, he's earning first reads and the passing volume should give him opportunities to make plays.

If you can't start him against this defense, what matchup are you waiting for? The opportunity is there. The matchup is there. This is the week he converts. — Ray Garvin

T.J. Hockenson catches 8 (or more) passes versus Lions' last-ranked TE defense

Kyle Murray remains vexed by the intermediate and deep passing game, but the short throws to Hockenson — the biggest guy on the field — can bail him out here. Hockenson's no longer a consistent week-to-week fantasy start, but he did catch 13 passes from Murray back in Week 4, and now he's up against a Detroit defense that's been horrible in seam coverage . Even if the volume doesn't perk up for Hockenson, he can pay off with a touchdown — Detroit's allowed a tight end spike in five of six games this year. — Scott Pianowski

Ja'Kobi Lane scores his first career touchdown

The rookie is a red-zone threat to say the least. In college, Lane scored 18 touchdowns on 99 receptions, mostly on targets inside the 20. With Lamar Jackson back, Lane's odds of scoring his first career touchdown shoot up. Since entering the NFL, Jackson has an astonishing 32.4% of his red-zone pass attempts go for a score, easily the highest in the league. Lane hasn't played much, but when he's been on the field he's been targeted, specifically in the red area, where his nine routes this season has got him six targets if you include a nullified touchdown catch. With Buffalo unable to slow down receivers this season, I expect the rookie to hit pay dirt in a shootout. — Joel Smyth

Makai Lemon has the most fantasy points among rookie WRs

There are a lot of emerging players right now, from KC Concepcion to Omar Cooper Jr. to Ja'Kobi Lane and so on. Lemon has had the quietest start, but his time to shine is now with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks out and Saquon Barkley limping. Lemon had his best game last week without them, finishing as the WR10 on WR17 expected half PPR points. He was targeted in ways that better suited his skill set, and Tanner McKee is just good enough to hit these underneath throws. The Eagles will need quick throws against an aggressive Commanders defense, and their corners aren't ones to fear. They've allowed the 7th-most fantasy points to WRs, and opposing offenses pass against them at the second-highest rate (60%) in neutral situations. — Hayden Winks

articles.title: Colorado Buffaloes fans in Halloween costumes rush field, tear down goalposts after OT win snaps losing skid
articles.summary: The Colorado Buffaloes snapped a five-game losing streak as Isaac Wilson's clutch overtime TD pass sparked a field-storming frenzy in Boulder.
articles.body: There hasn’t been much to be excited about in Boulder in regard to the Colorado Buffaloes’ football program lately. So, with an overtime victory to notch its first Big 12 win in over a year, the Buffaloes faithful decided it fitting to rush the field on Saturday afternoon. Deion Sanders’ Colorado squad came into their game against the Kansas State Wildcats 2-5 at the bottom of the barrel in the Big 12. To date, the team hadn’t won a conference game since Oct. 11, 2025, and they owned a five-game losing streak after beginning the year on a high note. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The game was tied at 21 apiece when four quarters finished, forcing an overtime period that saw Kansas State kick a field goal to take a three-point lead. If Colorado was able to find the end zone on the ensuing possession, they would snap that losing streak and finally get that first conference win of the year. On third-and-9, quarterback Isaac Wilson pulled back the ball on an RPO scheme and looked to throw into the end zone. He fired a bullet to tight end Charlie Williams, who snagged the football out of the air and walked into the end zone for an 11-yard score — his only catch of the game. With the six points, Colorado sent the stadium into a frenzy as it walked off Kansas State and improved to 4-4 on the season. As Sanders went to shake hands with Kansas State, fans hopped over the wall and stormed the field, most of them decked out in Halloween costumes. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Fans appeared ready to storm the field in regulation, but Kansas State’s touchdown with two seconds left tied the game and kept them behind the wall. Colorado eventually won, though, allowing fans to rush the field and, as is customary, tear down the goalposts while celebrating the spooky home victory. Colorado has matched its win total from last season in the fourth year of the Deion Sanders era. But despite the victory, Sanders’ name has been mentioned among coaches on the hot seat, making the modest milestone far from what he and his staff envisioned. The Buffaloes still have four games remaining this season, and they will need to win three of them to become bowl-eligible. If that happens, perhaps Sanders is safe moving forward into next year. If not… well, you do the math. There’s no telling what Colorado plans to do with Sanders, but the Buffaloes have struggled to regain their winning ways since his son, quarterback Shedeur Sanders, Heisman Trophy winner Travis Hunter and others left for the NFL. articles.title: Not even a chance at free tuition could get Maryland students in the seats for football Saturday
articles.summary: Maryland's free tuition giveaway failed to fill SECU Stadium as the Terrapins fell to Illinois 20-17 in a Halloween matinee with poor attendance.
articles.body: This week, Maryland announced plans to bolster poor football attendance by giving students who stayed until the final whistle a chance at free tuition. Surely, some partial relief from student loans would put butts in seats for a Halloween matinee against the Illinois Illini, right? Maybe kids aren't into free stuff like they used to be, because it certainly didn't. articles.title: New NHL Rumors Reveal Nikita Kucherov's Contract Asking Price Amid Lightning Trade Request
articles.summary: Nikita Kucherov stunned the NHL world when he requested a trade and told the Tampa Bay Lightning he wouldn't be signing an extension with them on Friday.
articles.body:
Nikita Kucherov stunned the NHL world when he requested a trade and told the Tampa Bay Lightning he wouldn't be signing an extension with them on Friday.

One day later, we have a better idea of what the star forward is seeking in a new deal.

According to The Athletic's Chris Johnston (h/t Eric Stephens ), Kucherov "is seeking a six-year contract with a $20 million average annual value." Such a deal would put him among the NHL's highest-paid players as contracts have skyrocketed over the last several months.

The 33-year-old is a Lightning legend, with the most points (1,142 points) in franchise history. His time in Tampa has included a pair of Stanley Cup titles, seven All-Star bids, three Art Ross Trophies (most points), two Hart Memorial Trophies (MVP) and two Ted Lindsey Awards (NHLPA's most outstanding).

He hasn't lost his proverbial fastball either—he has four goals and 11 assists in 12 games this season and is well on his way to eclipsing 100 points for a fifth straight season.

In other words, plenty of organizations would likely have interest in Kucherov if he was made available in a trade. The Lightning don't seem inclined to grant him that wish, however.

"We are aware of the media reports regarding the future of Nikita Kucherov with the Lightning," general manager Julien BriseBois said in a statement. "We unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita."

The Lightning risk losing him for nothing in unrestricted free agency over the summer. But with a talented but aging core still in place, the Lightning's window is slowly shutting, and it's understandable if they want to squeeze every last year out of it. So for now, Kucherov remains.

articles.title: Kelani Jordan vs. Wren Sinclair Winner, Top Highlights from NXT Halloween Havoc 2026
articles.summary: Kelani Jordan beat Wren Sinclair at Halloween Havoc on Saturday night to retain the NXT Women's Championship.
articles.body:
Kelani Jordan beat Wren Sinclair at Halloween Havoc on Saturday night to retain the NXT Women's Championship.

After years of trying, Jordan finally became NXT women's champion for the first time at Heatwave in August when she beat Sinclair's close friend, Kendal Grey.

A couple of weeks later, Sinclair attacked Jordan in an effort to get some revenge on Grey's behalf since Grey suffered an injury during her loss to Kelani.

While assaulting Jordan, Sinclair accidentally hit a referee in the face, which led to NXT general manager Robert Stone suspending Wren indefinitely.

During Sinclair's absence, Jordan had a successful title defense against Jaida Parker, and she suggested that no woman in the NXT locker room was capable of taking the NXT Women's Championship from her.

In order to determine her next challenger, Stone booked a 20-woman battle royal for the Oct. 6 episode of NXT with the winner going on to face Jordan for the title.

Shockingly, AAA luchadora Lady Shani appeared to win the battle royal by last eliminating Kali Armstrong.

However, when Shani removed her mask, it turned out that Sinclair was impersonating her, and she was the victor despite technically still being suspended.

Even though the legality of her win was disputed, Stone decided to uphold it and name Sinclair the No. 1 contender.

Sinclair had the chance to avenge Grey and become NXT women's champion for the first time on Saturday, but Jordan played spoiler and continued her reign in the process.

articles.title: Indiana survives Minnesota scare with second straight overtime win to keep national title defense alive
articles.summary: Grant Wilson's 25-yard TD pass to Charlie Becker on the first play of overtime lifted No. 4 Indiana past Minnesota in a dramatic Big Ten thriller.
articles.body: The fourth-ranked Indiana Hoosiers escaped again on Saturday. The defending national champions were able to breathe a collective sigh of relief after a 23-16 overtime victory over unranked Minnesota in its second consecutive overtime game. Last week, the Hoosiers won 13-6 at Michigan. INDIANA OUTLASTS MICHIGAN IN OVERTIME FOR FIRST WIN AT BIG HOUSE SINCE 1967 This week, backup quarterback Grant Wilson found Charlie Becker for a 25-yard touchdown on the first play of the extra period. The Hoosiers then stopped Minnesota on its ensuing possession. The Golden Gophers took a 16-13 lead with 19 seconds to go on Luke Drzewiecki’s career-long 60-yard field goal. But Charlie Becker’s 33-yard catch set up Paddy McAteer for a career-long 60-yarder to tie it as time expired. Minnesota fell to 0-13 against defending national champs and still has not beaten Top 25 opponents in back-to-back weeks since 1956. Indiana pulled struggling starting quarterback Josh Hoover at halftime after he took a big hit on his second interception of the season. Two late replay reviews then overturned potential game-changing plays: one erased a go-ahead touchdown pass, while the other nullified an interception that would have put Indiana deep in Minnesota territory in the final minutes. INDIANA SURVIVES NEBRASKA IN COMEBACK WIN, EXTENDS NATION'S LONGEST ACTIVE WINNING STREAK Wilson finished with 156 passing yards and a touchdown after Hoover recorded 119 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Becker caught eight passes for 149 yards and the game-winning touchdown. Minnesota quarterback Drake Lindsey completed 20 passes for 120 yards and one touchdown. Javon Tracy had seven receptions for 40 yards. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Minnesota will host No. 7 UCLA next Saturday, while Indiana will have a bye before hosting Southern California on Nov. 14. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Grayson Waller vs. Tony D'Angelo Winner, Top Highlights from NXT Halloween Havoc 2026
articles.summary: Grayson Waller defeated Tony D'Angelo at Halloween Havoc on Saturday night to retain the NXT Championship.
articles.body:
Grayson Waller defeated Tony D'Angelo at Halloween Havoc on Saturday night to retain the NXT Championship.

Shortly after the win, CM Punk challenged Waller for the NXT Title. The two will compete for the title next Wednesday.

D'Angelo won a Fatal 4-Way match at Stand & Deliver back in April to become NXT champion for the first time, but his reign came to an end after less than five months thanks to Waller.

In July, Waller made a shocking return to NXT after spending years on WWE's main roster. He cut a promo in which he called out the entire NXT men's division, and made it clear that he wanted to become NXT champion.

Waller accomplished his goal just one month later when he beat D'Angelo, Cruz Montana and Zilla Fatu in a Fatal 4-Way match for the NXT Championship at Heatwave.

D'Angelo quickly went to work trying to earn a rematch, but he initially hit a stumbling block when he lost a No. 1 contender's Triple Threat won by Mason Rook.

However, Rook was not medically cleared to compete against Waller, and after Waller successfully defended his title against EK Prosper, who stepped in for Rook, Tony D was back in the mix.

Both D'Angelo and Myles Borne confronted Waller and tried to get him to agree to put the NXT Championship on the line, and the Aussie Superstar decided to do so against the winner of a No. 1 contender's match between D'Angelo and Borne.

D'Angelo was victorious in that bout on the Oct. 13 episode of NXT, which made Waller vs. D'Angelo official for Halloween Havoc.

Defending the NXT Championship for the first time at an NXT premium live event, Waller prevailed and denied D'Angelo the chance to become a two-time NXT champion.

articles.title: BYU survives unranked Arizona State's second-half rally, stays unbeaten at home
articles.summary: Bear Bachmeier's clutch fourth-down conversions and 236 passing yards powered No. 8 BYU to a Big 12 victory after Arizona State erased a 14-point deficit.
articles.body: Eighth-ranked BYU pulled away after Arizona State rallied to tie the game at 17 late in the third quarter. Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier threw for 236 yards and a touchdown to help secure the 27-20 victory. The Cougars blanked the Sun Devils in the fourth quarter. After a 45-yard field goal put BYU ahead for good, running back Sione Moa scored from 1 yard out to seal the victory with just over two minutes remaining. Arizona State quarterback Jake Fette finished the late afternoon with 166 yards and two touchdowns, but the Sun Devils suffered their third road loss to a top-10 opponent this season. TRANSFER PORTAL, NOT NIL, REASON FOR PARITY, CLAIMS COLLEGE FOOTBALL EXPERT BROOKS AUSTIN Fette threw two third-quarter touchdown passes as Arizona State erased a 14-point deficit. The Sun Devils converted three third downs on their first scoring drive, which ended with Omarion Miller’s 20-yard touchdown catch. They then converted two fourth downs on the next drive before Anthony Miller Jr.’s 1-yard scoring reception tied the game at 17. Adrian Wilson recovered a fumble by Kyler Kasper at the BYU 39-yard line, setting up Arizona State’s second touchdown drive. It was a turbulent start for Fette in his first career start. BYU QB BEAR BACHMEIER SAYS NOTRE DAME 'DISRESPECTED' HIM AND HIS FAMILY FOLLOWING UPSET WIN OVER IRISH He fumbled on the third play of Arizona State’s opening drive. Isaiah Glasker pounced on the ball at the Sun Devil 29, setting up BYU’s first touchdown. Ironically, the Cougars scored following another fumble. Moa scooped up the ball after Bachmeier coughed it up inside the ASU 1 and scampered over the goal line to put BYU up 7-0. articles.title: Following illness, Tanvi battles tough Dakar conditions ahead of Youth Olympics
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Odisha’s Tanvi Patri hasn’t had the best preparation heading into the Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, where the badminton competition will be
articles.body: KOLKATA: Odisha’s Tanvi Patri hasn’t had the best preparation heading into the Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, where the badminton competition will be held from November 1-5.Drawn in Group F, the 15-year-old enters the tournament after falling ill at the World Junior Championships in Egypt earlier in Oct, where she suffered a Round-of-16 exit.“She wasn’t well for a week, but the rest after returning to India helped her recuperate. She then trained for a couple of days before travelling to Dakar, where she arrived on Oct 29,” her father Rabinarayan told TOI from Dakar on Saturday.“Of course, travelling and changing locations can be challenging, but overall, she is in good condition. We have been very careful with food, hydration and recovery. Those things become extremely important before a major tournament,” he added.However, conditions in Dakar have posed fresh challenges.“It’s very hot and there are lots of mosquitoes here. Also, since air-conditioners are not being provided, the athletes have to manage with just fans, which isn’t very helpful,” said Rabinarayan.Despite the difficulties, he remains confident of a strong showing from his daughter at her maiden Youth Olympics.“If you look at her performances in the last few tournaments, she has shown that she can compete at a high level even under difficult circumstances. Hopefully, things will continue to improve, and she will be able to give her best at the Youth Olympics,” he said.Although Tanvi fell short at the World Juniors, she has enjoyed an impressive season, winning her maiden senior title at the Pontianak International Challenge in Indonesia and finishing runner-up in Singapore before clinching the Asian U-17 girls’ singles crown in Chengdu, China.Her focus now, however, is firmly on Dakar, where she will face Australia’s Smrithi Adepu, Mexico’s Sara Patricia Delgado Gonzalez and South Korea’s Jang Yu Jeong in the group stage.“There is no pressure as such. She has already played many high-level tournaments. If you look at events in Singapore, Indonesia and other major competitions, those were in many ways tougher than this event,” said Rabinarayan. “She has gained valuable experience from competing against strong international players, so she knows how to handle big occasions.”While Tanvi is expected to progress comfortably from the group, Rabinarayan believes her toughest test could come in the semifinals against a Japanese opponent. If she reaches the final, she could face China’s Zhang Yixin, the girls’ singles champion at the 2026 BWF World Junior Championships.Having already conquered the Asian U-17 stage and tasted success on the senior circuit this year, Tanvi now stands one good week away from putting the perfect finishing touch on a breakthrough season.And if she can overcome the challenges that have marked her journey to Dakar, a Youth Olympic medal could be the reward.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bill Belichick's UNC Tar Heels nearly upset top-ranked Miami before costly strip-sack
articles.summary: UNC's Billy Edwards Jr. threw for 341 yards and four touchdowns, but a costly strip-sack swung momentum as Miami escaped Chapel Hill still undefeated.
articles.body: Bill Belichick, the day his UNC Tar Heels were set to face the No. 1 Miami Hurricanes in Chapel Hill, was the center of more off-field noise regarding his relationship. This time, though, it was reported the 74-year-old actually ended things with 25-year-old Jordon Hudson over a year ago, per TMZ. They remain "committed to their business partnerships" and "remain close friends." Nonetheless, a game had to be played, and Belichick and UNC were certainly not thinking about his relationship status. They wanted to give Miami a run for their money. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Tar Heels came close to upsetting the Hurricanes, but they ran out of gas in the fourth quarter in a 38-35 loss to move to 4-4 on the season. Miami stayed undefeated, improving to 8-0 on the year and 6-0 in ACC play. No one expected Belichick's squad to be able to handle the Hurricanes, led by Mario Cristobal. But just as Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah continued his efficient play this season, Billy Edwards Jr. was matching him when the Tar Heels had the ball. Edwards threw for 341 yards on 28-of-34 through the air with four touchdown passes, including a 16-yard strike to Jordan Shipp to take a 21-17 lead — UNC’s first of the game — in the third quarter. From there, both teams were trading blows, and the lead, on the scoreboard. Miami responded with an 80-yard drive to retake their lead, 24-21, but UNC continued to fight on while crushing clock heading into the fourth quarter. Edwards led a 16-play, 75-yard drive capped with a touchdown run by Demon June from one yard out. There was a lot of time left in this ballgame, which Miami knew despite some shock of what UNC was doing to them at home. Mensah wasn’t fazed, though, as yet another touchdown drive came from the Hurricanes thanks to key catch-and-runs, including a 31-yard burst from star receiver Malachi Toney. Mark Fletcher Jr. regained the Miami lead with a two-yard run and 7:49 left on the clock. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The way this game was going, it seemed Belichick and UNC would have a chance if they were able to get the ball last. However, a grave error slammed the door shut on those chances. Edwards was strip-sacked by Marquise Lightfoot, and Miami recovered at the UNC 37-yard line. That was the defensive stop needed to swing the tides of momentum, and Mensah didn’t thwart that opportunity. Toney caught a nine-yard touchdown pass from his quarterback, and with a 10-point lead with 2:33 left to go, it was eventually the separation needed to leave Chapel Hill without Miami’s record being blemished. But it didn’t come without sweating until the end. UNC would score on the ensuing possession to make things interesting, as Edwards threw for his fourth touchdown of the game with 1:38 left to play. Then, needing to recover an onside kick, the Tar Heels actually came away with it — until a yellow flag was seen on the turf. Offsides was called. On the second try, UNC recovered again, but another flag negated it as a Tar Heels player hit the Miami player trying to recover the ball before crossing the necessary 10 yards. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD The third try was finally recovered by the Hurricanes, and they ran the clock out. Mensah threw for 274 yards and three scores, while rushing for 36 yards. Toney had two of those touchdowns, hauling in seven receptions for 75 yards. Fletcher also scored three total touchdowns.

articles.title: 'El juego por dentro': Javier Romero Achón desvela qué pasa por la cabeza de un jugador de pádel
articles.standfirst: Escúchalo gratis en Spotify, Ivoox, Apple Podcast, Omny, MARCA.com y Radio MARCA
articles.summary: Escúchalo gratis en Spotify, Ivoox, Apple Podcast, Omny, MARCA.com y Radio MARCA
articles.body: MARCA estrena el cuarto episodio de la segunda temporada de 'El Juego por Dentro' con Javier Romero Achón, director de marketing de Siux, empresa referente del pádel en España y a nivel mundial. Monitor de pádel y jugador, se enganchó a este deporte a raíz de la pandemia y antes trabajó tres años en Babolat. En el podcast repasa el pádel desde su lado mental y emocional, y explica por qué, a su juicio, es un deporte distinto al resto por su accesibilidad y por el peso de la pareja. Sobre la relación entre compañeros, lo primero que defiende es entender que "tu pareja no falla a posta". Distingue entre recriminar un error y cuestionar una decisión, como insistir en un remate que no se domina. Para dejar el ego fuera de la pista propone "conocerte a ti mismo y no intentar ser el protagonista del partido en todos los tiros". La paciencia es otro de los ejes. Asegura que los jugadores top 5 o top 10 mundial a los que ha preguntado le dan siempre el mismo consejo al aficionado: "no intentar ganar el punto donde no toca". Sobre la comunicación con el compañero, defiende que "es mejor pasarse de comunicar que quedarse corto", y compara la "capacidad de olvido" que exige el pádel con la del golf, porque tras un fallo hay que intervenir en el punto siguiente. Javier también explica la 'nevera', la estrategia de dejar "frío" al rival que está acertado y jugar todas las bolas posibles al otro, y la importancia de detectar patrones del contrario. Sobre Tapia y Coello, sin haber trabajado con ellos, destaca que son completísimos, que "minimizan muy bien sus debilidades" y que saben adaptarse a pistas rápidas y lentas, lo que los mantiene "un escalón por encima del resto". Entre las diferencias con otros deportes, Javier destaca la cercanía de los jugadores. Frente al fútbol, donde para ver entrenar al Real Madrid en Valdebebas hay que estar acreditado, esperar una jornada de puertas abiertas o verlo "desde muy lejos", en el pádel "puedes plantarte casi en la puerta de la pista a ver entrenar" a jugadores como Stupaczuk o Augsburger. Esa cercanía, explica, se traslada a la relación entre marcas y jugadores, aunque admite que no sabe cómo evolucionará cuando los jugadores ganen más fama. Javier asegura que desde los organismos de máxima competición se valora limitar los cambios de pareja, quizá con un modelo como el del fútbol, con mercado de verano y de invierno, porque afectan a jugadores, patrocinadores, marcas y aficionados, que pierden referencias a largo plazo. Admite que sus palabras podrían quedarse anticuadas en unos meses. En su faceta profesional, cuenta que en Siux construyen el posicionamiento de cada jugador a partir de su estilo de juego, con Franco Stupaczuk, "el rayo", como ejemplo, y que la cercanía entre jugadores y marcas hace que lo que se ve sea "muy real". Sobre las redes y las críticas, asegura que los jugadores de élite "prestan cero atención" a lo que se dice de ellos y comparte su fórmula con los haters: "ser lo más educado posible". Su mensaje final: hacer las tareas "de una en una" y centrarse "en lo que tú puedas controlar". El Juego por Dentro, el videopodcast de bienestar mental y emocional en el deporte, está disponible en las principales plataformas de podcast (Spotify, Ivoox, Apple Podcast, Omny…) y también en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA. Suscríbete gratis en tu plataforma habitual para no perderte ningún episodio. Mantiene una periodicidad quincenal, con nuevos episodios cada dos semanas en los que deportistas, exdeportistas, psicólogos y expertos en rendimiento comparten su experiencia sobre mentalidad, gestión emocional, presión, liderazgo y crecimiento personal. Una propuesta interesante para profundizar en cómo funciona la mente del deportista y qué hay realmente detrás del rendimiento.

articles.title: USC great Matt Leinart celebrates ‘big win’ for Trojans vs. Ohio State
articles.summary: The USC Trojans knocked off No. 2 Ohio State 30-18 on Saturday, marking their biggest win of the season. It was a great response from Lincoln Riley’s team af...
articles.body:
The USC Trojans knocked off No. 2 Ohio State 30-18 on Saturday, marking their biggest win of the season. It was a great response from Lincoln Riley's team after the disappointment of their 24-7 defeat to Wisconsin the previous week.

USC great Matt Leinart was quick to congratulate the Trojans for their major achievement.

"Big win for Usc!!!!!" Leinart wrote on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Leinart led the Trojans to the 2004 BCS national championship and won the Heisman Trophy that season as well. He finished with a 37-2 record as a starter for USC, and his No. 11 jersey was retired after his graduation.

USC's current quarterback, Jayden Maiava, wasted no time putting the Trojans in front as he throw a 69-yard touchdown to Trent Mosley in just the second play of the game. They finished the first quarter up 14-3 thanks to a Waymond Jordan run and didn't look back from there.

Maiava did not do much else of note after that play as he finished 15 of 22 for 222 yards and one touchdown. But after his two early turnovers in the loss against Wisconsin, the fact that he threw zero interceptions and managed the game well overall was notable.

Meanwhile, the Trojans defense still gave up 464 total yards to Ohio State's offense, which had freshman Luke Fahey starting at quarterback for the injured Julian Sayin. But they made just enough plays in the second half to keep the Buckeyes at bay.

The Trojans will now look to build off that big win against the Buckeyes, as they take on the reigning national champion Indiana Hoosiers next week.

articles.title: Flames Come Up Short Against Avalanche in Colorado
articles.summary: The Calgary Flames couldn’t carry their momentum from Friday night’s win into Colorado, falling 5-2 to the Avalanche on Saturday night.
articles.body:
The Calgary Flames couldn't carry their momentum from Friday night's win into Colorado, falling 5-2 to the Avalanche on Saturday night.

Calgary was coming off a 6-2 victory over the Seattle Kraken and had won six of its previous eight games heading into the second half of a back-to-back.

Recently recalled goaltender Arsenii Sergeev got the start between the pipes for the Flames, but faced an early deficit against one of the league's top offensive teams.

Colorado opened the scoring at the 14:13 mark of the first period. After picking up a loose puck in the high slot, Nathan MacKinnon fired a shot upstairs past Sergeev to make it 1-0.

The Avalanche added to their lead early in the second period on the power play. At 2:37, MacKinnon sent the puck to former Flame Nazem Kadri, who found Martin Necas with a perfect cross-seam pass. Necas made no mistake, beating Sergeev with a one-timer to make it 2-0.

Just over three minutes later, Colorado struck again. Cale Makar dangled around a Flames defender before sliding the puck to Artturi Lehkonen, who quickly fired it past Sergeev to extend the lead to 3-0.

The Avalanche weren't finished. On a two-on-one rush, Gabriel Landeskog flipped a pass across to Brock Nelson, who chipped the puck out of the air and into the net to give Colorado a commanding 4-0 advantage.

Calgary finally got on the board before the end of the second period. Mikael Backlund won a battle along the boards and sent the puck out to Joel Farabee. Farabee kicked it to his stick before sliding a shot past Mackenzie Blackwood to make it 4-1.

The Flames carried some momentum into the third period, with Martin Pospisil cutting the deficit to two early in the frame.

After a strong forecheck and a turnover forced on Ryan Strome, Pospisil found himself with the puck in front of the net and buried his opportunity past Blackwood to make it 4-2.

However, any hopes of a Calgary comeback were quickly answered by Colorado.

Moments later, Makar sent a shot toward the net that Lehkonen redirected past Sergeev for his second goal of the night, restoring the Avalanche's three-goal lead at 5-2.

1. Farabee continues to deliver offensively

Joel Farabee has been one of Calgary's most productive forwards lately. His goal against Colorado gives him 12 points in his last seven games, with five goals and seven assists during that stretch. He's providing consistent offence and becoming an important part of the Flames' attack.

2. Calgary connections make an impact for Colorado

There were a couple of familiar connections on the Avalanche scoresheet. Calgary-born defenceman Cale Makar recorded four assists, while Nazem Kadri added an assist against his former team. Both played important roles in Colorado's offensive performance.

Morgan Frost is now just one point away from reaching 200 career NHL points. The Flames forward is approaching another personal milestone as he continues to establish himself in Calgary's lineup.

articles.title: 'Just a series not a tournament': Pakistan PM trolled again for over the top celebration tweet after ODI tri-series win
articles.summary: Pakistan's PM faced heavy fan ridicule over a hyperbolic social media post celebrating the ODI tri-series final in Lahore.
articles.body:
Shehbaz Sharif's tweet praising Pakistan's tri-series win drew heavy trolling from social media users.

Pakistan chased down Sri Lanka's 326 with nine balls left in the Lahore final.

Fakhar Zaman's 127 and a crucial 94-run stand sealed the first home tri-series title.

Fans roast Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif for hyping up home tri-series win

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif posted a gushing congratulatory message on X after the cricket team lifted its first tri-series trophy on home soil on Saturday evening.

The post was meant to salute the national team, but it quickly became a talking point for the wrong reasons, with X users poking fun at the language he chose.

He called the result historic and spoke warmly of the side's resolve, and that choice of word is what many users seized upon.

The Prime Minister singled out experienced opener Fakhar Zaman for special praise, and he also mentioned two promising youngsters, Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz, who had played key roles in the chase.

"Congratulations, Pakistan! A historic victory over Sri Lanka in the Tri-Series Final at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore!" he wrote.

He then turned his attention to the players who shaped the result, starting with the senior batter and the two younger men who finished the job.

"An outstanding century by Fakhar Zaman, followed by a magnificent partnership between two promising young talents, Arafat Minhas and Hassan Nawaz."

He rounded off the post with a hopeful line about the future of the game in the country.

"Wishing Pakistan cricket many more such triumphs," he added.

Fans troll Shehbaz Sharif over his tri-series victory tweet

Reactions came in quickly, and most of them leaned towards sarcasm.

One user was fairly direct about the mismatch between the occasion and the message. @Abdullahhhh_56 wrote: "We win the series it's good, but That's embarrassing sir it's just a series not a tournament & you are tweeting on irrelevant tournament & useless series."

Another account tried to imagine where such enthusiasm could end. @yuvraj336841 joked: "Next post: Congratulations Pakistan for winning toss"

An Indian fan mocked, suggesting the Prime Minister must be thrilled by what looks like a rare achievement. @SauravRoy24, in a post translated from Hindi, said: "Even winning a series is a historic victory? Looks like Pakistan has done it for the first time, that's why their PM is so happy. No worries, let him be happy in this."

Some users questioned how the Prime Minister uses his time. @Anurag9793 asked: "What kind of guy is this, man? Does he have nothing else to do? He comes just to tweet congratulations to the team for winning useless matches."

The last reaction brought up an old Hong Kong Sixes result to make its point. @TanyaXharma wrote: "Winning a league match of Hongkong Sixes against INDIA is equal to winning a Tri series? 😭 Or @CMShehbaz will start to tweet on every victory of Pakistan? 🇵🇰🤣"

Why Shehbaz Sharif's tweet became a target for trolls

There is nothing wrong with a head of government congratulating a national team, and the Pakistan players certainly earned applause for chasing 326 in a final. The trouble lies in the size of the language, because calling a tri-series win a historic triumph invites people to measure it against bigger occasions, and the comparison rarely flatters.

Fans on social media are quick to notice such gaps, and in this case they had plenty of material. Pakistan have won series before, so the word historic stretched the point, and a Prime Minister who posts with such enthusiasm every time risks cheapening his praise for the moments that truly deserve it.

It is also worth noting that the trolling says as much about the wider rivalry as it does about the tweet. A post from an Indian or Pakistani leader about cricket rarely gets a neutral hearing, and the jokes arrived within minutes, many of them from fans who had not watched the match.

Still, the team should not be punished for the noise. Fakhar's century was brilliant, Arafat's cameo was thrilling and the young finishers kept their composure at home. A more measured message would have given the players the spotlight they deserved, and it would have left the critics with far less to say.

For all the latest cricket news, opinion, and commentary, and to share your voice, head to our Facebook , Instagram , and X (Twitter) pages.

articles.title: Braylon Edwards congratulates Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith on breaking his Big Ten TD record
articles.summary: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith made college football history Saturday, officially becoming the Big Ten Conference’s all-time leader in rece...
articles.body:
Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith made college football history Saturday, officially becoming the Big Ten Conference's all-time leader in receiving touchdowns. Smith snagged his 40th career touchdown catch during Ohio State's matchup against the University of Southern California Trojans, passing former University of Michigan Wolverines standout Braylon Edwards on the all-time list.

Passing a legend is always sweet, but doing it across rival lines makes the feat even bigger. Edwards had held the conference record with 39 touchdown catches since wrapping up his collegiate career in 2004. Shortly after Smith reached the milestone in Los Angeles, the former Michigan star put rivalry animosity aside to tip his cap to the Buckeye sensation in a video message.

"Just giving a shoutout to a young man who just took over the all-time lead in receiving touchdowns for the Big Ten," Edwards said. "Shoutout to Jeremiah Smith of, yeah that school down south in Columbus. Kudos to you, you're a young brother, you've been working hard, busting your butt, one of one, it's been fun to watch what you do."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The historic touchdown against USC capped off another landmark week for the standout wideout. Smith had tied Edwards' long-standing mark on Oct. 17 during Ohio State's 19-15 victory over the Indiana Hoosiers before claiming the top spot outright on Saturday. Entering the game with 52 receptions for 984 yards and 12 touchdowns on the year, he delivered when his team needed him most.

With 40 receiving scores now under his belt, Smith continues to rewrite record books at both the program and conference levels. The junior already holds Ohio State program records for career receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns, a historic trifecta he locked up earlier this season.

Seeing a Michigan icon like Edwards publicly salute the player breaking his record speaks volumes about Smith's generational impact. The Big Ten touchdown crown now officially belongs to Columbus, and Smith is still building his legacy.

articles.title: St. Augustine stuns No. 24 Edna Karr, snaps 35-game win streak
articles.summary: St. Augustine stunned No. 24 Edna Karr 52-14, ending the Louisiana powerhouse's 35-game winning streak behind a dominant performance.
articles.body:
Losing is not something Edna Karr (LA) has done in nearly three years as Louisiana's top-ranked team entered the ninth week of the season riding a 35-game winning streak.

That winning streak was shattered Saturday night in a way many would have never could have expected as St. Augustine (LA) crushed the Cougars 52-14 handing Edna Karr, the No. 24 team in the Super 25 rankings , its first loss since losing to Acadiana (LA) by six in the 2023 Division I Select Playoff Semifinals.

It's the first double digit loss for the Cougars since that same season where they lost to John Curtis Christian (LA) 41-7.

In front of a crowd of several thousand, the Purple Knights took out five years of frustration on the Cougars. St. Augustine last won in 2020 but has since suffered five straight five straight losses to Edna Karr including a pair of blowout losses last year with one being for a state championship.

The Purple Knights appeared bound and determined to not let that happen.

St. Augustine jumped out early and led 20-8 by the end the first quarter. Edna Karr would not score again until late in the fourth quarter with a running clock going.

With the game already in blowout territory, freshman safety Louis Brown III put the game away with just over two minutes remaining in the half returning an interception 99 yards to put the Purple Knights up 33-8 at the half.

Junior quarterback Jaelle Noble had the game of his life in the win. He had accounted for three total touchdowns by halftime and by the time the final whistle blew, had finished his evening having a hand in all six of St. Augustine's offensive touchdowns.

With the win, St. Augustine moves to 9-0 on the year. The Purple Knights close out the regular season at home on Nov. 6 at home against Archbishop Rummel (LA). Edna Karr will also be at home next week to close out the regular season hosting Jesuit (LA) on Nov. 5.

articles.title: Vikings Add Versatile Running Back for Lions Game
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have turned to DeeJay Dallas for their Week 8 NFC North showdown against the Detroit Lions. The post Vikings Add Versatile Running Back...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are bolstering their game-day group with DeeJay Dallas.

"The #Vikings have elevated RB DeeJay Dallas to the active roster for tomorrow's game," the Vikings posted on X on October 31.

Dallas is deserving of this opportunity, and it is a warranted move for the Vikings in Week 8 against the Detroit Lions. However, the decision has significant implications for this game and Dallas' future with the VIkings.

Dallas, 28, has 10 yards on three carries and four catches for 34 yards in six games with the Vikings this season.

This officially marks Dallas' third elevation from the practice squad.

The Vikings will have to sign him to their 53-man roster or find another option if need be in Week 9. Dallas entered the NFL as a fourth-round draft pick, taken 144th overall by the Seattle Seahawks in 2020.

He has also spent time with the Arizona Cardinals, Carolina Panthers, and Jacksonville Jaguars in his career.

Dallas has 3,657 all-purpose yards in his 90 games played, including two starts.

DeeJay Dallas Provides Insurance for Vikings

Dallas contributes on special teams, but he also provides insurance for the Vikings' backfield, even with Aaron Jones progressing non-participation to limited action to shedding his injury designation with a full session on Friday.

Jones, who turns 32 in December, has managed a knee injury since training camp. He got banged up again in Week 7 against the Indianapolis Colts .

Jones is indeed expected to play, but he is likely far from 100%, even without a designation.

"I don't think you can really say enough about Aaron Jones with what he's giving right now," The Athletic's Alec Lewis posted on X on October 30. "Exit last Sunday looked rough. Had already been dinged. Lack of depth almost demands having him, but significant what he's putting his body through to be available."

The Vikings got Jordan Mason back from IR last week. They also still have rookie sixth-round pick (198th overall) Demond Claiborne. The Vikings made Claiborne inactive last week in favor of elevating Dallas from the practice squad.

articles.title: The Avalanche's Quiet Superstar Is Making A Very Loud Statement
articles.summary: Artturi Lehkonen is putting up superstar numbers in a contract year, giving the Colorado Avalanche another compelling reason to get a new deal done.
articles.body:
DENVER — Artturi Lehkonen is in a contract year, and he's subtly — but not so subtly — telling the Colorado Avalanche to send the paperwork.

Lehkonen, 31, would never come out and say it. That's part of what makes him so intriguing.

After another multi-goal performance Saturday night against the Calgary Flames at Ball Arena, Lehkonen finds himself tied for second in the NHL in goals alongside none other than Edmonton Oilers superstar Leon Draisaitl.

Lehkonen is keeping pace with one of the league's most prolific goal scorers. He's also ahead of his own teammate, Nathan MacKinnon, as well as Connor McDavid in the goal column. McDavid, of course, has eight goals and 29 assists, but the company Lehkonen is keeping is impressive nonetheless.

And yet, you wouldn't know it from listening to him.

The Finnish winger is about as humble as they come, often deflecting attention away from his individual accomplishments and toward his teammates, the team's overall performance, or even a fortunate bounce here and there. In that regard, there's something familiar about him. He's reminiscent of MacKinnon, who has never been particularly interested in celebrating his own statistical achievements.

Lehkonen would much rather talk about the hockey than the numbers.

The Hockey News asked Lehkonen what it meant to find himself tied with Draisaitl, one of the biggest names in the sport.

His response? About as humble as you'd expect.

"Not too much, to be honest. I mean, there's still a lot of season left'" he stated after the game. "You don't really change your style of play or the way you approach the game just because you've had a good start offensively. I'm just playing the same style of hockey I've always played."

While his name continues to climb the league's scoring leaderboard, the Finnish winger isn't getting caught up in the individual recognition. He isn't changing his game, chasing numbers, or putting too much stock into where he stands among the NHL's best.

He's simply doing what he's always done.

And right now, that's producing at an elite level.

Through 14 games, Lehkonen has 12 goals and 15 assists for 27 points. That's nearly two points per game. If he maintained that production over an 84-game season, he'd finish with 72 goals, 90 assists, and 162 points.

Obviously, sustaining that kind of production over an entire season is an entirely different challenge. But the numbers illustrate just how extraordinary Lehkonen's start has been. A 72-goal pace would put him among the NHL's most prolific goal scorers, and it's not exactly the kind of production anyone expected from the Finnish winger entering the season.

Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar certainly isn't dismissing the possibility.

When asked whether he thought Lehkonen could sustain his current pace, Bednar pointed to the habits that have made the winger so effective.

"I don't know, a long time, but I think it could go a long time," Bednar said. "He just keeps doing the right things, going to the right areas of the ice, almost had another one tonight. He's playing the right way and playing hard, and you see, he gets rewarded for going to the net, stopping at the net."

Bednar isn't suggesting Lehkonen is suddenly doing something entirely different offensively. Rather, he's continuing to do the things that have made him such a valuable player in Colorado. He wins battles, gets to the difficult areas of the ice, establishes himself around the net, and makes life uncomfortable for opposing goaltenders and defensemen.

And that's perhaps the most encouraging part for Colorado. Lehkonen isn't relying on a complete change in his game to generate offense. He's being rewarded for doing what his coaches have always asked of him.

Bednar's assessment was simple: "He just keeps doing the right things."

For a player whose value has always extended beyond the scoresheet, the offensive explosion is an added bonus.

Lehkonen is someone the Avalanche can trust in virtually every situation. He can contribute on the power play, play responsibly defensively, get to the difficult areas of the ice, and deliver when the stakes are highest. His playoff experience and willingness to do the dirty work have made him an important part of Colorado's identity.

That's what makes his contract situation so intriguing.

Colorado knows what it has in Lehkonen. He's been an important piece of the team's success, and his ability to produce offensively while maintaining the hard-nosed, responsible style that has defined his game makes him especially valuable.

Now, with his offensive numbers putting him alongside some of the NHL's biggest stars, the conversation surrounding his next contract becomes even more interesting.

Lehkonen isn't going to make a public pitch for himself. He doesn't need to.

The production is speaking for itself. And if his latest stretch is any indication, the Avalanche have another pretty compelling reason to get that paperwork moving.

articles.title: Recap: Avs snuff Flames in 5-2 triumph
articles.summary: It was an all treat no trick kind of night on Halloween.
articles.body:
It was a night where there were more treats than tricks as the Colorado Avalanche hosted the Calgary Flames on Halloween night. The game began well after the candy was handed out but Colorado tasted the sweet 5-2 victory at the end of the night. Artturi Lehkonen continued his hot streak with two goals and Cale Makar finished with four assists.

To start this game, the Avalanche generated many shots but no goals until Nathan MacKinnon broke through with just over five minutes remaining in the first period. A rebound found it's way right to MacKinnon in his favorite spot on the left side and he nailed the post and it bounced into the net behind Arsenii Sergeev making his second career NHL start for the Flames. Calgary got a few good looks on Mackenzie Blackwood but he shut the door especially on Matt Coronato by making a sprawling save with eight seconds to go to preserve the 1-0 lead.

On this Halloween night things got scary as the Avalanche received a power play early in the second period. As the first unit remained on the ice for nearly the full duration, Martin Nečas finally scored from the left circle and continued his hot streak of scoring on Halloween.

Minutes later, Arturri Lehkonen continued his own hot streak scoring his 11th goal on the season and Brock Nelson soon after. At that point the game entered garbage time as the clock began approaching midnight both on the evening and this game. Calgary tried to make it interesting when Joel Farabee made a spin move at the net front and finally got on the board to make it 4-1. Nothing much else happened in the period except for Brock Nelson got hit in the head on a Cale Makar shot but he returned to the bench by the start of the third period.

Speaking of the final frame, Colorado was feeling generous when a Brent Burns turnover behind the net led to a Martin Pospisil goal. Two minutes later, however, the Avalanche got it back as a Cale Makar shot was deflected by Lehkonen for his 12th goal of the season. Not much else happened other than Fedor Svechkov got chopped in the face and had to leave the ice for repairs and the Avalanche got a four-minute power play but they couldn't cash in. Therefore the 5-2 score stood at the final horn and Colorado secured their victory.

Lehkonen is on pace for 72 goals this season after scoring his 12th in 14 games. Never mind that it's on 28 shots on goal or what the ramifications of this will be but the Avalanche will take a hot streak to help them in the standings right now.

The four points he generated tonight is a sesson-high for Cale Makar. His high mark previous to this was a three-point effort when the Avalanche visited the Flames earlier in the month. That's nearly half of the 15 points Makar has on the year courtesy of Calgary. The Avalanche don't see the Flames again until April so Cale will have to find a new favorite team to play against.

The start of another quick road trip featuring a back-to-back. The fun begins on Monday, November 2nd at the Chicago Blackhawks. Puck drop is at 6 p.m. MT.

articles.title: Texas Southern wins again in walk-off fashion, this time to beat Grambling
articles.summary: Athean Renfro ran for two long touchdowns and Cam'Ron McCoy scored the winning TD in overtime as Texas Southern found itself in yet another tight game.
articles.body:
Cam'Ron McCoy ran for the winning touchdown in overtime as Texas Southern beat Grambling 23-20 on Saturday night at Thorne Stadium.

Athean Renfro led TSU with 232 yards rushing on 21 carries, including TD runs of 75 and 86 yards, to take the battle of Tigers squads.

McCoy's 6-yard run on the second possession of overtime gave TSU (3-5, 2-3 SWAC) its second straight walk-off win. Last week, TSU beat Southern on a field goal as time expired. Four of the Tigers' past five games have been decided by one score.

Grambling (4-4, 2-3) had tied the score with 4:46 left in the fourth quarter on Ashton Frye's 6-yard TD pass to Lantavious Murphy.

Grambling led 10-3 after three quarters before TSU tied the score and then took the lead on TD runs by Renfro 2:43 apart early in the fourth.

McCoy threw for 115 yards on 6-of-15 passing and added 46 yards rushing on 11 carries.

TSU stays home to face Alabama State at 2 p.m. Saturday at Thorne Stadium.

articles.title: Panic Meter: Are Ohio State’s College Football Playoffs chances doomed without Julian Sayin?
articles.summary: The Ohio State Buckeyes lost 30-18 to the USC Trojans on the road, in a game that they were forced to play without star QB Julian Sayin, who is out indefini...
articles.body:
The Ohio State Buckeyes lost 30-18 to the USC Trojans on the road , in a game that they were forced to play without star QB Julian Sayin , who is out indefinitely with an undisclosed right throwing arm and shoulder injury. Coach Ryan Day did not sound optimistic recently when discussing Sayin's chances of a return this season, choosing to plead the fifth on possible timetables on a week when Luke Fahey took over and helped Jeremiah Smith set another record .

The Buckeyes are looking like a team in danger of falling out of the College Football Playoffs chase with a record of 6-2 and the revenge-minded, Dan Lanning-led Oregon Ducks coming to the Horseshoe in Columbus for Week 10.

Is it time for Buckeyes fans to press the panic button? And are their Playoff dreams DOA? The Buckeyes need to keep a close eye on their Matt Patricia-led defense after giving up 30 points on the road to the Trojans.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Matt Patricia is a former NFL defensive coordinator and head coach and his coaching style is a great indicator of his experience. He knows how to dial up the right plays at the right time and put his defense in position to win.

The Buckeyes' Patricia-led defense wasn't completely gashed by the Trojans, but it did give up big games to the three-headed monster of Jayden Maiava, King Miller and Trent Mosley, which was troublesome.

Fahey just started his first game, and performed well all things considered with no interceptions and over 200 yards passing. If Fahey can keep up his conservative and smart play, the Bucks can beat everyone left on their schedule with running and defense.

Luke Fahey became just the fifth true freshman to start at QB in the Buckeyes storied program's history, a monumental achievement. He looks wise beyond his years and he knows how to rely on the running game with offensive coordinator Arthur Smith watching over him.

Program insiders have praised Fahey for his "moxie" and he will need more of it to keep pace with Lanning's Ducks after their huge comeback win over a revitalized Northwestern team.

Fahey could help the Buckeyes sink or swim, but the most likely outcome is that he will do his best to not lose games as the Buckeyes try to win it in other ways. The Buckeyes' passing game has enough playmakers that all Fahey has to do is get them the ball on short routes and they can make something out of nothing.

The Buckeyes are a huge question mark among college football teams, but that can be said about several other teams heading down the stretch of the season.

This year seems like the perfect one for a 24-team College Football Playoff, but it won't happen so the margin-for-error is slim in the Buckeye State.

If the Buckeyes can get past the Oregon Ducks in Week 10, they have a great chance to make the Playoff. If not, the season could spiral into something no one expected at the start of the season as Fahey and his teammates attempt to salvage a mid-tier to higher-tier bowl game before the regular season fully runs its course.

articles.title: What Bill Belichick said about UNC football onside kicks vs Miami
articles.summary: UNC football recovered back-to-back onside kicks, but penalties prevented the Tar Heels from attempting a comeback. Here's what Bill Belichick had to say.
articles.body:
CHAPEL HILL — UNC football recovered consecutive onside kicks in the final two minutes against No. 1 Miami , but consecutive penalties negated the recoveries in a 38-35 loss .

"It's probably about right," UNC coach Bill Belichick said. "They're both close. They looked close to me."

On the first onside kick, Shamar Easter was called offside. On the second onside kick, Peyton Seelmann was tagged with an illegal block.

"That was pretty tough," Seelmann said. "A little upsetting that we didn't get either of them. It's what the refs called and it's what happened."

Seelmann felt the Tar Heels (4-4, 2-3 ACC) were "gonna go win it" before the officials revealed the penalties.

"It's 'cause the ball didn't go 10 yards yet and I hit him," Seelmann said of the blocking penalty.

But UNC had to kick a third onside kick and the top-ranked Hurricanes (8-0, 6-0) recovered it, eventually entering to victory formation to escape Kenan Stadium with their undefeated record still intact.

"I don't know, I kind of just assumed the ball was right there because I saw him go like this," Seelmann said, opening his hands. "I just went out to hit him a little too early."

UNC scored touchdowns on five of its seven drives, but a strip-sack fumble allowed Miami to take a double-digit lead in the final minutes. The Hurricanes scored on six of their seven possessions, punting once with five touchdowns and a field goal.

articles.title: Lennart Karl’s late substitution for Bayern Munich was not a form issue
articles.summary: Lennart Karl showed a flash of his old self in the vital Der Klassiker game for FC Bayern.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich had several opportunities to bring Lennart Karl into Der Klassiker against Borussia Dortmund, but stand-ion coach Aaron Danks only brought him on with six minutes left. Considering his recent return from injury and the fact that he is still in search of his form, is Karl ready for more playing time in big games like these?

Bayern had to substitute off Ismail Saibari and Serge Gnabry in the first half against Dortmund. They were replaced by attack-minded fullbacks in Nathaniel Brown and Alphonso Davies, while Lennart Karl was brought on only in the 84th minute. Assistant coach Aaron Danks was asked whether this was due to a lack of readiness for a big game.

"Lennart Karl came on in the second half, so we trust him in these games, for sure. He came on for Michael, on the right wing, and played exactly the same role that he does," answered Danks (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) reaffirming his confidence in the youngster.

"Prior to that, Alphonso Davies playing high on the left wing for us has been a good option over the recent weeks, so we decided to go with that one. And Nathaniel Brown played in the attacking midfield position against Dortmund in Dortmund in the Super Cup at the start of the year, so we brought him on in that position. That's nothing against Lenny. Lenny is a top player; he came on the pitch, he had a great moment at the end where he hits the crossbar, just really positive for him, " Danks added, highlighting the priority placed on continuity.

The final few minutes where Kane played with Davies, Brown, and Karl will likely form Bayern's attack until the rest of the attackers return from injury. This combination showed great spirit in the final minutes and an ability to change pace and direction quickly, with all four players having a keen eye for goal. Staying fit and maximizing this rare opportunity is easily Karl's top priority. If he can build back his rhythm and confidence, he has the potential to tear it up in Germany and Europe this season.

articles.title: Tyrese Maxey admits he is tired of the 76ers having to come back from big deficits
articles.summary: Tyrese Maxey and the 76ers had to pull off another comeback in their latest win.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a superb start to the 2026-27 NBA season, with a 6-1 record. This comes after their latest win against the Charlotte Hornets , 109-104. It was not an easy victory because they had to come back from a double-digit deficit yet again.

That was the fourth time they had to claw back from a double-digit deficit, so it seems that the 76ers are well aware of that problem. They do not want that to become an issue, so they are ready to put that behind them.

Tyrese Maxey does not want the 76ers to get complacent after another comeback

The 76ers have been one of the most impressive teams this season, as they are actually living up to the hype. The same cannot be said for some teams this season, but the 76ers do know they are not a perfect team.

They have started with six wins and a single loss, but there could be some problems with how they approach games. The 76ers have the tendency to let the opponent take a big lead, then they rely on a big run to come back and win the game.

While that leads to some satisfying wins, it is not the most sustainable approach to games. The 76ers need to establish themselves from the jump, so they can win comfortably. It seems that star player Tyrese Maxey has the same sentiment.

"I don't want to do that; I'm tired of that. This group some fighters, man. We went up, went down, came back, you know, we're very competitive. The game's not over 'til it's over, and that's what I really like about this group," Maxey said in his post-game interview after the win against the Hornets .

With all of the awesome players the 76ers have on the roster, they are ready to win and be healthy. If they can have more comfortable results, they can afford to rest some of their star players. Maxey would love that, as they are building better contuinity for their goals of winning a title.

articles.title: Is Iowa Football Dr. Jekyll Or Mr. Hyde?
articles.summary: Iowa picked up a monster win over Wisconsin one week after a heartbreaking loss to Minnesota. Now eight games in, […]
articles.body:
Iowa picked up a monster win over Wisconsin one week after a heartbreaking loss to Minnesota.

Now eight games in, and we still are unsure what to make of Iowa football.

The Hawkeyes suffered a heartbreaking 13-10 loss to Minnesota back on October 24. But on Halloween, Iowa looked like monsters vs. Wisconsin.

Hank Brown had over 200 yards passing and the defense pitched a shutout, posting a 30-0 victory.

Iowa Goes As The Offense Does Just Like Every Other Year

When it comes to Hawkeye football, you know the defense is going to be strong. They allowed just 13 points in the loss to Minnesota. And even though Ohio State put up a season-high 31, they still played relatively well.

So, which version of the offense are we going to get next week when they travel to Northwestern?

Brown, who has returned to the role of starting quarterback, had time to work. He hit on 20 of 24, throwing for 222 yards with two touchdowns.

Brown found Tony Diaz four times for 75 yards and a score, connecting with DJ Vonnahme for the other touchdown. Reece Vander Zee had five receptions and four others caught passes.

Iowa also gave Brown a sound – not great – run game. The Hawkeyes rushed for 140 yards, and did have multiple runs of over 10 yards.

The Hawkeyes Now Have Three Shutouts, Top-Notch Defense

This year, Iowa has recorded three shutout victories and rank in the Top 10 in the country in scoring defense. They allowed just 52 rushing yards, and have now outscored Wisconsin the last two years, 72-0.

When Iowa can control the line of scrimmage, they have just enough talent at the skill positions to do damage. The Hawkeyes cannot overcome turnovers or long down-and-distance plays, but they can play well within themselves.

After playing a Northwestern team coming off a loss to Oregon on the road, Iowa closes with Purdue, Illinois and Nebraska. Needless to say, those are all winnable games for this version of the Hawkeyes.

Michigan took on Rutgers at the SHI Stadium in New Jersey on Saturday. While the Wolverines started hot, scoring a touchdown on their very first drive, Rutgers answered back in the second quarter with a touchdown of their own.

As Rutgers tied the game shortly after with a touchdown and a two-point conversion, fans took to social media to express their discontent with Butkowski after he missed six points that could have been crucial for the Wolverines.

"Trey Butkowski should be walking home."

"STOP SENDING BUTKOWSKI OUT THERE OH MY GOSH HE'S THE WORST KICKER IN MICHIGAN HISTORY WHY HAS HE NOT BEEN BENCHED???!!!"

Tommy Carr Showed Out in Win vs. Rutgers

Michigan quarterback Tommy Carr wasn't the most popular man on the Wolverines squad after a disappointing offensive performance against Indiana, but he redeemed himself against Rutgers.

Carr threw for 266 yards on 22-of-27 completions and a touchdown, while adding 54 yards and two rushing touchdowns to his stat sheet as Michigan survived a late Rutgers comeback in a dominant fourth quarter.

Running back Savion Hiter tallied 76 yards on 20 carries, adding to the dominant run game as the Wolverines rushed for 161 yards total while dominating time of possession. The Wolverines improved to 5-3 and will face archrivals Michigan State next on Nov. 7.

articles.title: Another Blonde Ole Miss Fan Goes Viral Moments Before Trinidad Chambliss Touchdown
articles.summary: Crowd shots do not seem to stop going viral on social media during Ole Miss game days. An ABC cameraman panned to a fan in the stands early in the fourth qua...
articles.body:
Crowd shots do not seem to stop going viral on social media during Ole Miss game days. An ABC cameraman panned to a fan in the stands early in the fourth quarter against Auburn, and the clip was circulating fast before the Rebels finished a 45-15 win. It landed two plays before Trinidad Chambliss threw a touchdown.

This is becoming a pattern for Ole Miss games. Sara Smith went viral in the September 6 opener against Louisville, holding her phone overhead as the Cardinals scored. Three weeks later, an ABC cameraman drew accusations of lingering on a fan in the stands during Florida's 52-28 win.

"The cameraman doing his job and finding the most attractive white blonde for the nation to see on national TV during the Ole Miss vs Auburn game," An X handle by the name MAGA Elvis captioned a video on X . The video showed a fan in a light-blue top waving a rag with one arm while others in light blue stand behind her, showing a Saturday crowd shot from a noon kickoff in Oxford.

The shot came two plays before Chambliss hit Caleb Cunningham for a six-yard touchdown, and Ole Miss was already up 24-15. The Rebels were close to putting it away, and the broadcast was cutting to the stands instead of the field.

TV directors constantly look for these crowd shots to keep fans engaged during stoppages. For major networks like ABC and ESPN, panning to reactions in the stands is a standard broadcast trick to build atmosphere, especially when a game feels like a blowout or momentum slows down. But when a camera zeroes in on the same fan profile game after game, social media turns a routine production cut into a trending topic.

Auburn had cut it to 17-15 on a Byrum Brown touchdown run, and Alex Golesh went for two and missed. Chambliss answered with a 26-yard touchdown run late in the third. Shekai Mills-Knight opened the fourth with a 10-yard run. Chambliss got a first down with his legs, and the drive covered 72 yards in 11 plays. Cunningham's score made it 31-15 with 12:33 left.

"So they came back in the second half and responded, but I thought it was a combination of early down success in the run game to get them behind the chains and then more importantly, the efficiency of us on offense," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said, according to Evelyn Van Pelt of RebelWalk.

"And I think they felt like, look, man, if we don't extend the drive and we don't score points, like their offense is going to score, and I think they get a little pass happy. So I think they threw it a lot more than the anticipation coming into it."

It did not look like that early. It was 14-9 at halftime, as Chambliss threw a first-half pick to AnQuon Fegans, and an Auburn extra point got blocked. After Cunningham's score, the Rebels hit a 28-yard touchdown pass to Horatio Fields and a 17-yard touchdown run from backup Deuce Knight, who was facing his former team.

Ole Miss scored the final 28 points, outgained Auburn 487-312 and rushed for 224 yards to Auburn's 63. The Rebels were 13-for-16 on third down. Chambliss finished 22-of-34 for 263 yards and two touchdowns, with 65 rushing yards and another score.

Mills-Knight got 16 carries for 71 yards with Kewan Lacy out, and he had 12 career carries coming in. Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) has won 16 straight at home and three in a row over Auburn (4-4, 2-4). The Tigers host Arkansas next.

Georgia comes to Oxford next Saturday on November 7. If the camera finds another fan in the stands against a top-three Georgia team, the internet will notice before the Rebels do.

articles.summary: Week 9 of the 2026 regular college football season sees the Ole Miss Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC) take on the Auburn Tigers (4-3, 2-3 SEC) at Vaught-Hemingway Stadi...

Week 9 of the 2026 regular college football season sees the Ole Miss Rebels (5-2, 3-2 SEC) take on the Auburn Tigers (4-3, 2-3 SEC) at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Mississippi, on Saturday.

As the first quarter ended scoreless, the pressure to get points on the board was intense heading into the second quarter. For Chambliss, this play added to his interception total this season.

With this interception, Chambliss has now accumulated eight interceptions and is at par with his LSU counterpart, quarterback Sam Leavitt, whom the college football world often compares him to. Both Leavitt and Chambliss are now tied for the most interceptions thrown by a quarterback in the SEC so far this season.

This infamous statistic for Chambliss has prompted fans online to call out his on-field display.

"This Trinidad Chambliss guy is a turnover MACHINE", wrote a fan on X.

"(Sam) Leavitt is already better than Chambliss if you were wondering", commented a fan on X.

At the time of writing, the Ole Miss Rebels lead the Auburn Tigers 24-15 late in the third quarter.

Which Quarterback Has the Most Interceptions in CFB 2026?

While the 2026 college football season has seen amazing moments on the field driven by quarterbacks, it has also seen plenty of misdirected passes and receiver fumbles that have led to more interceptions.

On a list no quarterback wants to top, Akron Zips quarterback Brayden Roggow leads with nine interceptions.

With Roggow leading this dreaded list, seven signal callers have thrown eight interceptions in the first nine weeks of this college football campaign, namely Ashton Daniels (Florida State Seminoles), Marcel Reed (Texas A&M Aggies), Sam Leavitt (LSU Tigers), JJ Kohl (FIU Panthers), Caden Creel (Jacksonville State Gamecocks), Jared Curtis (Vanderbilt Commodores), and Trinidad Chambliss (Ole Miss Rebels).

articles.title: Nets rule out Mikel Brown Jr. vs. Pacers during front end of back-to-back
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets will be without rookie point guard Mikel Brown Jr. during Sunday’s road matchup with the Indiana Pacers. They ruled out the No. 6 pick for...
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets will be without rookie point guard Mikel Brown Jr. during Sunday's road matchup with the Indiana Pacers . They ruled out the No. 6 pick for the front end of a back-to-back due to back injury management. Brown is expected to play on Monday against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

Brown has come off the bench for the Nets to start this season while on a minutes restriction. He won't play in back-to-backs until that restriction is lifted, which won't happen anytime soon, according to head coach Jordi Fernandez.

"Right now, we're building him up, and if you look at the schedule, we have two days in between [games]. So when you play this amount of minutes, you get assessed. Assessed is how you feel, everything," head coach Jordi Fernandez said after Brown played a season-high 28 minutes during Tuesday's loss to the Boston Celtics. "Then you have 48 hours, and then you play another game. And when he does it for the weeks that we have planned, which I'm not going to share with you guys, and we feel like he's strong enough and he's gone through it and that his body can assimilate all the load, [then he'll be off the minutes limit]. This was one game. He played more because we're confident that with the rest he has [upcoming]. So that's where we are. And right now it's the fourth game. [Mikel won't be off the limit] anytime soon because I want to load him with minutes and have him feeling good."

Brown scored 17 points during the fourth quarter and overtime during his season-high 28 minutes in Boston on Tuesday. He struggled to replicate that production while playing 23 minutes during Friday's 110-94 home loss to the Detroit Pistons.

A top-two team has fallen to an unranked opponent for the fourth consecutive week, and on Saturday, it was Ohio State football 's turn to suffer an unexpected defeat.
